newsitem.title: CANADA: Four killed, 18 wounded in Canada gas explosion.
newsitem.headline: Four killed, 18 wounded in Canada gas explosion.

text.p: A violent explosion thought to have been caused by a natural gas leak killed four people and injured 18 on Wednesday in a small western Canadian town, police said.

A police spokeswoman in Quesnel, British Columbia, about 250 miles (400 km) north of Vancouver said the explosion ripped through a small building in the town's commercial district early on Wednesday evening. The building then burst into flames, sending thick clouds of smoke through the area.

"A preliminary investigation indicates the explosion was likely caused by a gas leak," the police spokeswoman said. The building housed two businesses, a sports-card trading shop and a thrift store, and was next to a gasoline station.

Witnesses said the explosion sent glass flying and was felt for up to a mile (2 km). "It was a tremendous boom," Vic Spooner, who lives half a block from the scene, told the Canadian Press news agency.
Among those hurt were shoppers, people walking in the area and volunteers who went into the flaming building to rescue trapped victims.

"The front of the building was blown across the street and the other walls were blown out. One of the cars across the street was flipped," said Matt Williamson, who was nearby when the building ignited.
Local radio reported that five of the injured were seriously hurt and taken to hospitals in the regional centre of Prince George and Vancouver.
As the night wore on, rescuers used heavy machinery to remove debris as they searched for missing people, Canadian Press said.
Quesnel, which has a population of about 8,000, is in central British Columbia in a remote area known for logging and mining.
